title: A Phase-Field Model Coupled with Large Elasto-Plastic Deformation: Application to Lithiated Silicon Electrodes
one_sentence_summary: Chen et al. couple a free-energy-based Cahn-Hilliard phase field to finite J2 elasto-plasticity, showing in a lithiating silicon nanowire that a stable nanoscale phase front and chemical expansion constrained by the lithiated outer shell drive the surface hoop stress from compression into late-stage tension, while plasticity limits and redistributes stress.

study_identity.domain: Coupled phase-field, chemo-mechanics, and finite-deformation simulation of silicon lithiation
study_identity.evidence_mode: Thermodynamic formulation, finite-element case study, analytical interface-width check, and comparison with a prior diffusion model

module_alignment.module_title: CVD-deposited nanosilicon in micron-scale porous carbon
module_alignment.rationale: The paper studies an isolated silicon nanowire and contains neither porous-carbon geometry nor CVD deposition, so it contributes only transferable silicon-expansion mechanics.

module_alignment.module_title: Phase transformation, crystallization, and mechanical conditions in lithiated silicon
module_alignment.rationale: It directly couples crystalline-to-amorphous two-phase lithiation with stress and plasticity, but it does not model nucleation of a crystalline lithiated-silicon phase or derive a crystallization criterion.
This is the paper's central contribution: a Cahn-Hilliard concentration phase field is coupled to finite chemical-elastic-plastic deformation and mechanical equilibrium.

The model introduces a nanoscale diffuse-interface length inside a continuum FEM calculation, but no explicit parameter-transfer chain connects atomistic, particle, electrode, cell, and experimental scales.

one_sentence_conclusion.text: A free-energy-based phase-field model coupled to finite J2 elasto-plasticity preserves a stable nanoscale lithiation front and predicts that constrained chemical swelling drives the silicon-nanowire surface from early hoop compression to late hoop tension.

why_worth_reading.text: It provides a compact, reusable example of how to connect phase separation, stress-dependent chemical potential, large chemical expansion, plasticity, boundary conditions, and finite-element implementation in one thermodynamically consistent model.

research_problem.text: The paper asks how a sharp crystalline-Si/amorphous-LixSi lithiation front, roughly 300% local volume expansion, plastic flow, and evolving stress can be simulated together without losing a physical interface thickness under large deformation.

prior_gap.text: Earlier large-deformation silicon models generally treated lithiation as single-phase diffusion, whereas earlier phase-field models used small-strain elasticity or lacked a demonstrated high-capacity-electrode implementation.

core_contribution.text: The authors derive and implement an arbitrary-geometry finite-element framework that combines a conserved concentration phase field, multiplicative chemical-elastic-plastic kinematics, concentration-dependent elasticity, J2 plasticity, and quasi-static mechanics.

scope_boundary.text: The conclusions apply to an idealized isotropic, traction-free circular nanowire with prescribed surface lithiation and assumed plastic parameters; the study does not simulate fracture, reaction kinetics, anisotropy, porous carbon, CVD manufacture, or a cross-scale parameter-transfer workflow.

research_object.text: The modeled object is the first lithiation of a crystalline silicon nanowire, where a Li-rich amorphous LixSi shell advances inward across a diffuse interface into a nearly unlithiated crystalline core.

geometry_and_scale.text: The numerical case uses a circular nanowire cross-section with a 70 nm reference radius; symmetry reduces the calculation to a two-dimensional quarter-domain.
The phase boundary is treated as a diffuse nanoscale interface whose analytical equilibrium width is 1.12 nm.

phases_and_composition.text: A single normalized lithium concentration field distinguishes a Li-poor crystalline-Si state from a Li-rich amorphous LixSi state; the Li-rich free-energy minimum is set at c-hat = 0.872.
The concentration field therefore represents both local composition and phase identity, rather than using a separate structural order parameter.

process_and_loading.text: Lithium enters from the exterior surface, forming an expanding Li-rich shell whose interface moves radially toward the nanowire center.
There is no externally applied mechanical load; stress develops internally from constrained chemical expansion under a traction-free outer boundary and symmetry constraints.

state_variables.text: Primary fields are normalized lithium concentration, chemical potential, and two displacement components; plastic deformation is retained as a history-dependent internal state.
Derived quantities include deformation factors, radial and hoop stress, von Mises stress, accumulated plastic strain, interface position, and interface width.

target_outputs.text: Resolve the evolving core-shell concentration morphology and verify that the phase boundary retains a material-controlled thickness during large swelling.
Predict how radial and hoop stresses and plastic strain evolve as the lithiation front advances, especially the late-stage surface hoop-tension relevant to cracking.

framework.text: The formulation couples conserved Cahn-Hilliard phase evolution to finite chemical-elastic-plastic kinematics and quasi-static mechanical equilibrium in the reference configuration.

assumptions.text: One scalar normalized concentration represents both lithium content and the crystalline/amorphous phase state.
Chemical expansion is isotropic, elastic properties vary with concentration, and irreversible deformation follows volume-preserving isotropic J2 plasticity with linear hardening.
Mechanical relaxation is fast relative to diffusion, so quasi-static force balance holds at every transport time step; plastic free energy is assumed independent of concentration.

free_energy.text: Total free energy combines a non-convex chemical double well, elastic strain energy, plastic energy, and a concentration-gradient penalty.

The double well stabilizes Li-poor and Li-rich compositions, while the gradient coefficient and barrier height jointly determine interface energy and width; elastic energy makes chemical potential sensitive to deformation and stress.

governing_equations.label: Total free energy and chemical potential
governing_equations.explanation: The variational derivative converts chemical, gradient, and mechanical energy changes into the lithium transport potential; under the stated assumption, μ_pl = 0.

governing_equations.label: Conserved phase-field evolution
governing_equations.explanation: Mass conservation and mobility-driven flux give a Cahn-Hilliard equation for inward motion of the two-phase lithiation front.

governing_equations.label: Mechanical equilibrium
governing_equations.explanation: The first Piola stress satisfies quasi-static balance in the reference configuration at every time step.

constitutive_relations.label: Multiplicative deformation split
constitutive_relations.explanation: Chemical swelling, plastic flow, and recoverable elastic distortion are separated so very large lithiation deformation does not imply unrealistically large elastic strain.

constitutive_relations.label: Isotropic chemical expansion
constitutive_relations.explanation: Lithium concentration produces an isotropic volumetric eigen-deformation calibrated to the assumed fully lithiated volume increase.

constitutive_relations.label: J2 plasticity with linear hardening
constitutive_relations.explanation: Deviatoric yielding limits the stress generated by chemical swelling, while accumulated plastic strain raises the subsequent yield threshold.

coupling_logic.text: Concentration changes chemical free energy, mobility, elastic properties, and chemical expansion; deformation changes elastic energy and therefore the chemical potential that drives lithium flux.
Lithium transport advances the phase front, local expansion generates stress and plastic flow, and the resulting elastic state feeds back into transport through μ_el.

parameters.name: Reference nanowire radius
parameters.role: Sets the particle geometry and radial diffusion distance.

parameters.name: Li-rich normalized concentration
parameters.role: Defines the lithiated free-energy minimum and imposed surface composition.

parameters.name: Analytical interface width
parameters.role: Provides the intrinsic-length validation target for the phase-field solution.

parameters.name: Fully lithiated volume ratio
parameters.role: Represents a 300% volume increase caused by chemical expansion.

parameters.name: Yield strength
parameters.role: Controls the onset of irreversible deformation in the lithiated silicon.

parameters.name: Linear hardening modulus
parameters.role: Controls the growth of flow resistance with accumulated plastic strain.

parameters.name: Physical time step
parameters.role: Sets the implicit temporal discretization used in the reported simulation.

initial_conditions.text: The quarter nanowire begins nearly Li-poor and stress-free, with the prescribed initial concentration profile and undeformed reference geometry.

boundary_conditions.text: The exterior concentration is fixed at the Li-rich value, while the normal chemical-potential flux is zero.
The outer mechanical surface is traction-free and the two cut faces use displacement symmetry conditions for the quarter-domain.

numerical_implementation.text: COMSOL solves a split form of the fourth-order phase-field equation as two second-order equations coupled to mechanical equilibrium.
The spatial discretization uses two-dimensional three-node triangular elements with four nodal degrees of freedom: concentration, chemical potential, and two displacements.
Time advancement uses a first-order implicit scheme, and the converged fields are postprocessed for front position, interface width, stresses, and plastic strain.

reproducibility_check.text: The paper provides the governing formulation, principal parameters, geometry, boundary conditions, element type, degrees of freedom, software, and time step, which is sufficient to reconstruct the benchmark in principle.
Exact mesh density, nonlinear-solver tolerances, complete weak-form implementation, input files, and downloadable COMSOL model are not available, preventing bitwise reproduction.

key_results.text: A sharp Li-rich shell advances inward while the unlithiated crystalline core shrinks; the front slows during later lithiation.
Plastic yielding limits and redistributes stress, and the outer-surface hoop stress changes from early compression to late tension.
The simulated diffuse-interface width remains close to the 1.12 nm analytical value throughout lithiation.

validation_and_comparison.text: The computed core-shell concentration morphology is qualitatively consistent with in-situ observations of two-phase lithiation in crystalline silicon nanowires.
At matched front positions, radial and hoop stress profiles broadly agree with a prior nonlinear concentration-dependent diffusion calculation, although small numerical fluctuations remain.

The strongest internal quantitative check is agreement between the simulated interface width and the analytical phase-field estimate; there is no matched spatially resolved experimental stress validation.

mechanistic_interpretation.text: When the surface first lithiates, its chemical expansion is constrained by the inner core, producing hoop compression and plastic flow in the outer shell.
As lithiation continues beneath the already expanded shell, the advancing interior expansion stretches that shell circumferentially, reversing the surface hoop stress into tension.
The balance between the double-well barrier and gradient penalty prevents numerical spreading of the phase boundary and gives the model a stable intrinsic length scale.

sensitivity_and_uncovered.text: Plastic-range parameters were selected as representative values because measurements were unavailable; the paper compares elastic and elastoplastic responses but does not systematically sweep yield strength, hardening, mobility, gradient energy, or mesh size.
The study does not resolve fracture, surface oxide, defects, crystallographic anisotropy, electrochemical reaction kinetics, contact constraints, cycling, or porous composite architecture.

experimental_correspondence.text: The predicted moving crystalline-core/amorphous-shell morphology corresponds qualitatively to reported in-situ nanowire observations.

The late tensile surface state supplies a plausible cracking mechanism, but the model neither propagates a crack nor compares the stress history with a measured fracture threshold for a matched specimen.

module_value.text: For CVD nanosilicon in porous carbon, the reusable part is the finite-deformation silicon constitutive framework; pore geometry, carbon constraint, interface adhesion, and deposition morphology must be added.

For lithiated-silicon phase mechanics, the paper shows how stress and plasticity interact with a crystalline-to-amorphous front, but it does not establish the mechanical conditions for nucleating a crystalline lithiated phase.

For phase-field–mechanics–electrochemistry simulation, it is a central reference because it gives the free energy, governing transport, finite-deformation kinematics, plastic law, coupling path, boundary conditions, and FEM realization in one example.

For multiscale simulation, the intrinsic interface length can serve as a lower-scale-informed continuum parameter, but a full atomistic-to-particle-to-electrode-to-cell transfer and experimental closure are absent.

reusable_elements.text: Reusable model elements include the total free-energy decomposition, stress-sensitive chemical potential, split Cahn-Hilliard implementation, multiplicative chemical-elastic-plastic kinematics, and J2 plastic update.
Reusable verification cases include the analytical 1.12 nm interface-width check, the quarter-circle symmetry benchmark, and comparison of elastic versus elastoplastic surface-stress histories.

limitations_and_next_steps.text: Extend the domain to silicon deposited inside a resolved porous-carbon skeleton, including Si-C contact, adhesion or slip, pore confinement, and spatially varying deposition thickness.

Replace prescribed surface concentration with reaction kinetics and electrolyte transport, calibrate constitutive and phase-field parameters against experiments or lower-scale calculations, and add fracture and cycling damage.
Perform mesh and time-step convergence and parameter sensitivity studies before using predicted stresses quantitatively for design.

reproducibility_verdict.text: The paper is conceptually reproducible and suitable for rebuilding the benchmark, but only partially computationally reproducible because executable model files, complete solver settings, mesh-convergence evidence, and calibrated plastic data are unavailable.

paper_profile.rationale: The central contribution is a thermodynamically derived coupled formulation; its finite-element realization is a reusable method, and silicon-nanowire lithiation supplies the engineering application.

gap.text: Existing large-deformation silicon models usually represented lithiation as single-phase diffusion, while earlier phase-field treatments used small-strain elasticity or lacked a demonstrated high-capacity-electrode implementation; neither combination reliably retained a physical phase-boundary thickness under large plastic swelling.

core_contribution.text: The paper integrates a conserved concentration phase field, finite chemical-elastic-plastic kinematics, and quasi-static mechanics so that Li transport, phase-front motion, deformation, and stress evolve together in an arbitrary-geometry FEM framework.

method_logic.text: A double-well chemical energy selects Li-poor and Li-rich states, the gradient penalty sets interface energy and width, elastic energy makes chemical potential stress-sensitive, and J2 flow accommodates irreversible swelling; the variational potential then drives Cahn-Hilliard transport while mechanical equilibrium is solved at every time step.

decisive_evidence.text: The inward concentration front stays sharp and slows between later snapshots, demonstrating that the formulation represents two-phase propagation rather than smooth single-phase filling.
Stress profiles broadly match the earlier nonlinear-diffusion calculation at two matched front positions, while the surface hoop stress reverses sign late in lithiation.
The simulated interface width remains close to the 1.12 nm analytical estimate throughout lithiation, supporting the claimed intrinsic length scale.

limitations.text: The demonstration assumes an isotropic circular nanowire, prescribed Li-rich concentration at the surface, zero potential flux, and a traction-free boundary; anisotropy, reaction control, and realistic contacts are absent.
Yield and hardening parameters were chosen as typical values because plastic-range properties were unavailable, and the numerical stress curves retain small fluctuations.

future_work.text: The clearest next step is a systematic calculation of how stress modifies Li diffusion and interfacial reaction rates, which the authors explicitly leave outside this study.
The physical-space FEM formulation is positioned for complex electrode shapes and boundary conditions beyond the circular nanowire benchmark.

quick_read.text: The state variable is normalized Li concentration c-hat; one conserved field simultaneously distinguishes Li-poor crystalline Si from Li-rich amorphous LixSi and tracks local lithiation.

The governing transport law is a Cahn-Hilliard equation driven by chemical/gradient and elastic contributions to chemical potential; although the formal decomposition includes a plastic term, it vanishes because the paper assumes plastic energy is independent of normalized concentration. Multiplicative finite-deformation kinematics and J2 plasticity govern the mechanical response separately.
COMSOL solves the split second-order phase-field equations and mechanical equilibrium on a quarter-domain triangular mesh with implicit first-order time integration.
The model predicts a sharp inward-moving front and a late switch of surface hoop stress from compression to tension because the lithiated shell constrains expansion at the moving front.

Its strongest quantitative validation is the nearly constant diffuse-interface width around the 1.12 nm analytical value; stress validation is comparative rather than a direct fit to spatially resolved experiment.

central_claims.claim: A phase-field formulation can couple two-phase lithiation to large elasto-plastic deformation while preserving an intrinsic interface thickness.
central_claims.evidence_summary: The free-energy gradient term supplies a length scale, and the computed boundary width remains near the analytical 1.12 nm estimate throughout the simulated lithiation history.
central_claims.what_it_proves: For the stated free energy, parameters, and nanowire problem, the discretized model maintains a physically interpretable, nearly stationary diffuse-interface width.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not establish that the same parameters or interface law quantitatively predict every silicon morphology, crystallographic orientation, or cycling condition.
central_claims.open_question: How should gradient energy and double-well parameters be calibrated independently for different silicon phases and temperatures?

central_claims.claim: The cracking-relevant surface load path has two stages: early compression is partly accommodated by J2 yielding, then continued subsurface lithiation stretches the previously lithiated shell like a membrane and leaves it in hoop tension.
central_claims.evidence_summary: The surface stress begins compressive, plastically yields, and then becomes tensile as the already-lithiated shell constrains expansion at the advancing internal front.
central_claims.what_it_proves: The coupled model produces a mechanically plausible sign reversal under its axisymmetric loading and boundary conditions.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: The calculation does not resolve crack nucleation or propagation and does not quantify a fracture threshold against a matched specimen.
central_claims.open_question: Does the predicted tensile history exceed measured fracture resistance when surface defects, oxide, and electrochemical reaction kinetics are included?

pipeline.text: Represent lithiation and the crystalline/amorphous distinction with the conserved normalized concentration c-hat, and prescribe a double-well chemical free energy whose Li-rich minimum is at 0.872.

Decompose total deformation into chemical, plastic, and elastic factors; compute stress with concentration-dependent elasticity and evolve irreversible deformation using isotropic J2 flow with linear hardening.
Differentiate the total free energy to obtain chemical potential, use its gradient for Li flux, and combine flux with conservation to form the stress-coupled Cahn-Hilliard equation.
Split the fourth-order phase-field equation into two second-order equations and solve them with mechanical equilibrium by FEM at each implicit time step.

method_understanding.algorithm_pseudocode:
Initialize c-hat and deformation on a quarter nanowire.
At each time step, solve the split concentration/potential equations and quasi-static displacement equilibrium with constitutive updates.
Advance c-hat and plastic state; record phase-front position, geometry, and stresses.

algorithm_steps.action: Initialize the quarter-domain nanowire with the prescribed concentration profile and stress-free geometry.
algorithm_steps.inputs: Radius, initial c-hat, material and phase-field parameters
algorithm_steps.outputs: Initial concentration, displacement, and plastic state

algorithm_steps.action: Apply saturated Li-rich concentration, zero potential flux, symmetry constraints, and traction-free exterior mechanics.
Solve chemical potential, concentration conservation, and mechanical equilibrium in weak form with constitutive plastic updates.
algorithm_steps.inputs: Current concentration, deformation, and plastic history
algorithm_steps.outputs: Updated c-hat, chemical potential, displacement, and stress

algorithm_steps.action: Advance implicitly and extract front location, interface width, stress components, and accumulated plastic strain.
algorithm_steps.outputs: Time-resolved phase, morphology, stress, and plasticity results

engineering_derivation_sketch.text: Start with a free energy that penalizes mixed compositions and concentration gradients while adding deformation-dependent elastic and plastic energies. Under the paper's assumption that plastic energy is independent of normalized concentration, its derivative contributes mu_pl=0; chemical/gradient and elastic terms therefore form the active Li potential. Onsager-type flux down that potential, combined with mass conservation, yields Cahn-Hilliard evolution. Multiplicative kinematics separately tracks chemical swelling, recoverable elasticity, and plastic flow without assuming small strain.

implementation_details.text: The implementation uses COMSOL, 2D three-node triangles, four nodal degrees of freedom (concentration, chemical potential, and two displacement components), and implicit first-order time integration.
A quarter circular domain exploits symmetry; the reference radius is 70 nm and the physical time step is 2.45 s.

problem_formulation.text: The problem is to evolve a sharp but diffuse Li-rich/amorphous shell into a Li-poor/crystalline silicon nanowire core while accounting for approximately 300% local swelling, plastic flow, and stress-modified chemical potential.

key_equations.label: Stress-coupled Cahn-Hilliard evolution
key_equations.latex:
G=\int[f_{ch}(\hat c)+f_{el}(F,\hat c)+f_{pl}(F)+ rac{\kappa}{2}|
abla\hat c|^2]d\Omega_0;\quad \mu=\mu_{ch}+\mu_{el}+\mu_{pl},\;\mu_{pl}=\partial f_{pl}/\partial\hat c=0;\quad \partial_t\hat c=
abla\cdot(M_{Li}(\hat c)
abla\mu)
key_equations.explanation: Chemical and gradient terms create two phases and a finite interface, while elastic energy makes μ stress-sensitive. Plastic energy appears in the formal free energy but does not directly drive transport here because its concentration derivative is assumed zero.

key_equations.label: Diffuse-interface width
key_equations.explanation: The width is set by the competition between gradient penalty κ and the double-well barrier Δg; this supplies the material length scale missing from the comparison diffusion model.

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: Defines chemical potential from the derivative of the total free energy.
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: Li moves in response to the energetic cost of composition gradients, phase preference, and mechanical loading rather than concentration alone.

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: Separates chemical swelling, plastic flow, and elastic distortion.
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: Large irreversible shape change can be represented without forcing the elastic strain itself to become unphysically large.

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: Converts a sharp discontinuity into an energetically controlled diffuse interface.
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: The gradient penalty prevents an arbitrarily thin numerical jump, while the double well favors the two bulk compositions.

assumptions.text: One scalar concentration field represents both composition and amorphous/crystalline state, despite the two quantities being conceptually distinct.
Chemical expansion is isotropic, plastic flow is volume-preserving J2 plasticity with linear hardening, and stress relaxes quickly enough for mechanical equilibrium at every diffusion time.
The outer surface remains saturated at the Li-rich concentration and traction-free, with zero normal potential flux.

key_results.text: The model produces a persistent core-shell phase morphology and an inward front whose motion slows at later time.
The interface width remains approximately 1.12 nm, whereas the comparison nonlinear-diffusion model lacks a stable material length scale.
The surface hoop stress reverses from compression to tension as the lithiated shell restrains interior expansion.

engineering_proof_sketch.text: The non-convex chemical energy fixes two preferred concentrations, and the gradient term fixes the transition cost; their balance gives the analytical interface width. As Li-rich material forms at the outside, chemical swelling generates compression and plastic flow there. Continued inward advance expands material beneath an already swollen shell, turning the shell's circumferential stress tensile. Solving mechanics and chemical potential together makes this stress history alter the transport driving force.

limitations.text: The regular-solution expression is used only as a mathematical double well and is not claimed as a microscopic free energy for amorphous LixSi.
Stress-dependent diffusion and reaction retardation are present in the framework but not systematically investigated in the reported calculations.

task_context.text: The application targets first lithiation of a crystalline silicon nanowire, where an amorphous Li3.75Si-rich shell advances into a nearly unlithiated crystalline core across an approximately nanometer-scale boundary.

experimental_setup.text: The numerical benchmark uses a 70 nm-radius circular cross section and compares concentration-front behavior with in-situ observations and stress fields with a prior nonlinear concentration-dependent diffusion model.
The Li-rich composition is set to c-hat=0.872, elasticity softens with lithiation, and the model uses 1.5 GPa yield strength and 1.0 GPa hardening modulus.

constraints.text: Axisymmetry, isotropy, uniform surface saturation, and traction-free mechanics suppress crystallographic, reaction-front, contact, and defect heterogeneity.

transfer_limits.text: The equations can be extended to other high-capacity phase-changing electrodes, but the silicon-specific free energy, mobility, plastic parameters, and boundary conditions require recalibration before quantitative transfer.

datasets.text: No dataset is introduced; validation uses an idealized 70 nm silicon-nanowire calculation, qualitative in-situ core-shell observations, an analytical interface-width estimate, and a prior nonlinear-diffusion simulation.

metrics.text: Evaluation examines phase-front position and sharpness, interface width, radial/hoop/von Mises stresses, stress sign history, and accumulated plastic strain.

main_results.text: The phase field sustains a sharp core-shell front, reproduces stress-profile trends from the nonlinear-diffusion model, and predicts surface hoop tension at late lithiation.
The computed interface width stays close to its analytical value over time instead of broadening severalfold as reported for the comparison diffusion formulation.

ablation_or_comparison_takeaways.text: Elastic versus elasto-plastic curves show that yielding strongly limits stress magnitudes and changes their time evolution, making plasticity essential for the large-swelling silicon case.
Residual differences from the nonlinear-diffusion stress profiles are attributed to different plasticity laws, mesh density, and geometry; small phase-field stress fluctuations remain.

numeric_results.dataset_or_task: Two-phase lithiation of a 70 nm-radius silicon nanowire
numeric_results.baseline: Analytical estimate from gradient energy and double-well barrier
numeric_results.comparison: Phase-field width remains close throughout lithiation
numeric_results.interpretation: The diffuse interface retains the intended nanoscale material length rather than spreading continuously with time.
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: Agreement with the internal analytical estimate is not an independent calibration of κ or Δg for all silicon electrodes.

numeric_results.dataset_or_task: Constitutive setup for fully lithiated silicon
numeric_results.metric: Final-to-initial volume ratio implied by 300% volume increase
numeric_results.comparison: Used to set chemical expansion coefficient beta=0.5874
numeric_results.interpretation: The finite-deformation formulation is exercised at four times the initial material-point volume, the large-swelling regime relevant to silicon lithiation.
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: A prescribed expansion does not validate the constitutive law or its path dependence against a specific experiment.

code.evidence: No code repository is identified in the local article, and the single permitted DOI landing-page check was blocked before an official external artifact could be assessed.
code.notes: The paper names COMSOL as the implementation platform but does not provide source code in the inspected local text.

data.evidence: The work reports simulation curves rather than a released research dataset; no official data package could be checked because the DOI page was inaccessible to the lookup.
data.notes: Parameters are printed in Table I, but reusable input or output files were not identified.

models.evidence: The mathematical model is documented in the paper, but no downloadable COMSOL model or other executable model artifact was verified.
models.notes: The external DOI lookup was blocked by robots.txt.

parser_limitations: The paper index assigns many body paragraphs to page 1, so visual page numbers were verified against rendered page images.
Several displayed equations are omitted or degraded in parsed text; governing relations were checked against page 5 and the interface-width equation against page 7.
missing_sections: No dedicated fracture calculation or experimental methods section is present because cracking is interpreted from computed stress rather than simulated directly.
low_confidence_equations: The compact free-energy equation summarizes the paper's displayed functional and does not reproduce every Jacobian factor in its reference-configuration expansion.
visual_crop_limitations: Only full-page renderings were available, so all visual cards are approximate page views rather than tight figure crops.
external_info_used: A direct lookup of DOI 10.1149/2.0171411jes was attempted on 2026-08-17 and blocked by robots.txt; no external availability claim was inferred beyond that result.

zh.one_sentence_summary: Chen 等将基于自由能的 Cahn–Hilliard 相场与有限变形 J2 弹塑性耦合，针对硅纳米线锂化表明：稳定的纳米级相界面以及受已锂化外壳约束的化学膨胀会使表面环向应力由早期压缩转为后期拉伸，而塑性负责限制并重新分配应力。

research_overview.one_sentence_conclusion: 基于自由能的相场模型与有限变形 J2 弹塑性耦合后，既能维持稳定的纳米级锂化界面，也预测受约束的化学膨胀会使硅纳米线表面环向应力由早期压缩转为后期拉伸。
research_overview.why_worth_reading: 这篇文章给出了一个紧凑且可复用的范例：如何在同一套热力学一致模型中连接分相、应力相关化学势、大化学膨胀、塑性、边界条件和有限元实现。
research_overview.research_problem: 论文要解决的问题是：在大变形条件下，如何同时模拟尖锐的晶态 Si/非晶 LixSi 锂化界面、约 300% 的局部体积膨胀、塑性流动与演化应力，并保持具有物理意义的界面厚度。
research_overview.prior_gap: 既有硅大变形模型通常把锂化视为单相扩散，而早期相场模型多采用小应变弹性，或尚未在高容量电极上给出完整数值实现。
research_overview.core_contribution: 作者推导并实现了适用于任意几何的有限元框架，综合守恒浓度相场、化学—弹性—塑性乘法分解、浓度相关弹性、J2 塑性和准静态力学平衡。
research_overview.scope_boundary: 结论基于各向同性、外表面无牵引、表面浓度给定的理想圆形纳米线，并采用假设的塑性参数；文中没有模拟断裂、界面反应动力学、各向异性、多孔碳、CVD 制造或跨尺度参数传递。

research_system.research_object: 研究对象是晶态硅纳米线的首次锂化：富锂非晶 LixSi 壳层跨越弥散界面向近乎未锂化的晶态核心推进。
geometry_and_scale: 数值算例采用参考半径 70 nm 的圆形纳米线截面，并利用对称性缩减为二维四分之一计算域。
相界面被处理为纳米尺度弥散界面，其解析平衡宽度为 1.12 nm。
phases_and_composition: 单一归一化锂浓度场区分贫锂晶态硅与富锂非晶 LixSi，富锂自由能极小值设为 ĉ=0.872。
因此浓度场同时表示局部化学组成和相身份，没有另外引入结构序参量。
process_and_loading: 锂从外表面进入，形成膨胀的富锂壳层，相界面沿径向向纳米线中心推进。
模型没有施加外部机械载荷；应力来自化学膨胀的内部约束，外表面无牵引，切面施加对称约束。
state_variables: 主要求解场为归一化锂浓度、化学势和两个位移分量；塑性变形作为具有历史依赖的内部状态保存。
派生量包括变形分解、径向与环向应力、von Mises 应力、累积塑性应变、界面位置和界面宽度。
target_outputs: 解析演化中的核壳浓度形貌，并验证大膨胀过程中相界面仍保持由材料参数控制的厚度。
预测锂化界面推进时径向应力、环向应力和塑性应变的演化，重点关注与开裂相关的后期表面环向拉应力。

model_and_mechanisms.framework: 模型在参考构形中将守恒 Cahn–Hilliard 相场演化、有限化学—弹性—塑性运动学与准静态力学平衡耦合。
assumptions: 一个归一化浓度标量同时表示锂含量和晶态/非晶态相状态。
化学膨胀各向同性，弹性性质随浓度变化，不可逆变形采用体积不变、线性硬化的各向同性 J2 塑性。
力学松弛相对于扩散足够快，因此每个输运时间步都满足准静态平衡；塑性能被假设为与浓度无关。
free_energy: 总自由能由非凸化学双阱、弹性应变能、塑性能和浓度梯度惩罚项组成。
双阱稳定贫锂和富锂组成，梯度系数与势垒高度共同决定界面能和界面宽度；弹性能使化学势受到变形和应力影响。

governing_equations.label: 总自由能与化学势
governing_equations.explanation: 变分导数把化学能、梯度能和机械能变化转化为锂输运势；按照文中假设，μ_pl=0。

governing_equations.label: 守恒相场演化
governing_equations.explanation: 质量守恒与迁移率驱动通量共同给出 Cahn–Hilliard 方程，用于描述两相锂化界面向内推进。

governing_equations.label: 力学平衡
governing_equations.explanation: 第一 Piola 应力在参考构形中满足准静态平衡，并在每个时间步求解。

constitutive_relations.label: 变形梯度乘法分解
constitutive_relations.explanation: 分别描述化学膨胀、塑性流动和可恢复弹性畸变，从而避免把巨大锂化变形错误地解释为巨大弹性应变。

constitutive_relations.label: 各向同性化学膨胀
constitutive_relations.explanation: 锂浓度产生各向同性体积本征变形，其幅值按完全锂化的假定体积增量标定。

constitutive_relations.label: 线性硬化 J2 塑性
constitutive_relations.explanation: 偏应力屈服限制化学膨胀产生的应力，累积塑性应变则提高后续屈服阈值。

coupling_logic: 浓度改变化学自由能、迁移率、弹性性质和化学膨胀；变形改变弹性能，进而改变驱动锂通量的化学势。
锂输运推动相界面，局部膨胀产生应力和塑性流动，新的弹性状态再通过 μ_el 反馈到输运过程。

parameters.name: 纳米线参考半径
parameters.role: 规定颗粒几何和径向扩散距离。

parameters.name: 富锂归一化浓度
parameters.role: 规定富锂自由能极小值和表面施加的组成。

parameters.name: 解析界面宽度
parameters.role: 作为相场解内禀长度的验证目标。

parameters.name: 完全锂化体积比
parameters.role: 表示化学膨胀导致的 300% 体积增量。

parameters.name: 屈服强度
parameters.role: 控制锂化硅开始发生不可逆变形的条件。

parameters.name: 线性硬化模量
parameters.role: 控制流动阻力随累积塑性应变的增长。

parameters.name: 物理时间步长
parameters.role: 规定文中隐式时间离散的推进尺度。

initial_conditions: 四分之一纳米线起始时近似贫锂且无应力，采用给定的初始浓度分布和未变形参考几何。
boundary_conditions: 外表面浓度固定为富锂值，同时化学势法向通量为零。
外部机械表面无牵引，四分之一域的两个切面施加位移对称条件。
numerical_implementation: COMSOL 将四阶相场方程拆为两个二阶方程，并与力学平衡联立求解。
空间离散采用二维三节点三角形单元，每个节点具有浓度、化学势和两个位移共四个自由度。
时间推进采用一阶隐式格式，收敛场用于提取界面位置、界面宽度、应力和塑性应变。
reproducibility_check: 论文给出了控制框架、主要参数、几何、边界条件、单元类型、自由度、软件和时间步，原则上足以重建基准算例。
论文未提供精确网格密度、非线性求解容差、完整弱形式实现、输入文件和可下载 COMSOL 模型，因此无法逐位复现结果。

key_results: 尖锐的富锂壳层向内推进，未锂化晶态核心逐渐缩小，界面在锂化后期减速。
塑性屈服限制并重新分配应力，外表面环向应力由早期压缩转为后期拉伸。
模拟弥散界面宽度在整个锂化过程中保持接近 1.12 nm 的解析值。
validation_and_comparison: 计算所得核壳浓度形貌与晶态硅纳米线两相锂化的原位观察定性一致。
在匹配的界面位置上，径向和环向应力分布与既有非线性浓度相关扩散计算总体一致，但仍存在小幅数值波动。
最强的内部定量校核是模拟界面宽度与相场解析估计一致；文中没有针对匹配试样的空间分辨应力实验验证。
mechanistic_interpretation: 表面最初锂化时，其化学膨胀受到内部核心约束，使外壳产生环向压应力和塑性流动。
锂化继续向已膨胀外壳下方推进时，内部新增膨胀沿环向拉伸外壳，使表面环向应力反转为拉伸。
双阱势垒与梯度惩罚的平衡抑制相界面的数值扩散，为模型提供稳定的内禀长度尺度。
sensitivity_and_uncovered: 由于缺少测量，塑性区参数采用代表性数值；论文比较了纯弹性与弹塑性响应，但没有系统扫描屈服强度、硬化、迁移率、梯度能或网格尺寸。
研究未解析断裂、表面氧化层、缺陷、晶向各向异性、电化学反应动力学、接触约束、循环过程或多孔复合结构。
experimental_correspondence: 预测的移动晶态核心/非晶壳层形貌与已有纳米线原位观察定性对应。
后期表面拉伸状态提供了合理的开裂机理，但模型没有扩展裂纹，也没有与匹配试样的实测断裂阈值比较。

module_value: 对于多孔碳中 CVD 纳米硅，有限变形硅本构可以复用，但必须加入孔结构、碳约束、界面黏结或滑移以及沉积厚度分布。
对于锂化硅相变力学，论文展示了应力和塑性如何作用于晶态到非晶态界面，但没有给出锂化硅晶相的形核力学条件。
对于相场—力学—电化学仿真，这是一篇核心参考，因为它在同一算例中给出了自由能、输运方程、有限变形运动学、塑性定律、耦合路径、边界条件和有限元实现。
对于多尺度仿真，内禀界面长度可以作为低尺度信息进入连续体模型的参数，但文中没有原子—颗粒—电极—电芯的完整传递和实验闭环。
reusable_elements: 可复用的模型内容包括总自由能分解、应力相关化学势、拆分式 Cahn–Hilliard 实现、化学—弹性—塑性乘法分解和 J2 塑性更新。
可复用的验证算例包括 1.12 nm 解析界面宽度校核、四分之一圆域对称基准，以及纯弹性与弹塑性表面应力历程对比。
limitations_and_next_steps: 把计算域扩展到解析的多孔碳骨架内部沉积硅，加入 Si—C 接触、黏结或滑移、孔隙约束及空间变化的沉积厚度。
用界面反应动力学和电解液输运替代表面定浓度，通过实验或低尺度计算标定本构与相场参数，并加入断裂和循环损伤。
在把预测应力用于定量设计前，需要完成网格与时间步收敛以及参数敏感性研究。
research_value_resources.reproducibility_verdict: 该论文在概念层面可复现，适合重建基准算例；但由于缺少可执行模型、完整求解设置、网格收敛证据和标定后的塑性数据，计算层面只能部分复现。

quick_read: 状态变量为归一化锂浓度 ĉ；同一个守恒场既区分贫锂晶态硅与富锂非晶 LixSi，也描述局部锂化程度。
输运方程是 Cahn–Hilliard 方程，化学势的有效驱动力来自化学/梯度项与弹性项；形式分解虽然包含塑性项，但由于论文假设塑性能与归一化浓度无关，μ_pl=0。乘法有限变形运动学与 J2 塑性则单独控制力学响应。
COMSOL 在四分之一圆域的三角形网格上求解拆分后的二阶相场方程和力学平衡，时间积分采用一阶隐式格式。
模型给出向内推进的尖锐相界面；由于已锂化外壳约束内部移动界面处的继续膨胀，表面环向应力在后期由压缩转为拉伸。
最有力的定量验证是弥散界面宽度始终接近 1.12 nm 的解析值；应力部分主要与既有模型比较，而非直接拟合空间分辨实验。

argument_map.gap: 既有大变形硅模型通常把锂化视为单相扩散，早期相场工作则多采用小应变弹性或缺少在高容量电极上的数值实现，因而难以在大塑性膨胀下同时保持具有物理意义的相界面厚度。
argument_map.core_contribution: 论文把守恒浓度相场、有限化学—弹性—塑性运动学和准静态力学平衡整合起来，使锂输运、相界面移动、形貌变形与应力能够在任意几何的有限元框架中共同演化。
argument_map.method_logic: 双阱化学能选择贫锂与富锂状态，梯度能规定界面能与宽度，弹性能使化学势受到应力影响，J2 流动则容纳不可逆膨胀；由变分得到的化学势驱动 Cahn–Hilliard 输运，每个时间步同时求解力学平衡。
decisive_evidence: 浓度界面向内移动且始终尖锐，后期移动距离变小，说明模型描述的是两相界面推进而非平滑的单相填充。
在两个相同界面位置处，相场模型与非线性扩散模型的应力分布总体一致，同时表面环向应力在锂化后期发生符号反转。
模拟界面宽度在整个锂化过程中接近 1.12 nm 的解析估计，支持模型具有内禀长度尺度。
limitations: 算例假设各向同性圆形纳米线、表面固定为富锂浓度、化学势零通量且外表面无牵引，未包含晶向、反应控制和真实接触。
塑性区材料参数因缺少测量而采用典型值，数值应力曲线仍存在小幅波动。
future_work: 最直接的后续工作是系统量化应力对锂扩散和界面反应速率的影响，作者明确将其留待后续研究。
物理空间中的有限元实现可进一步用于比圆形纳米线更复杂的电极几何和边界条件。

central_claims.claim: 相场模型可在保持内禀界面厚度的同时，将两相锂化与大弹塑性变形耦合。
central_claims.evidence_summary: 自由能中的梯度项提供长度尺度，计算得到的界面宽度在整个锂化历程中保持在解析估计 1.12 nm 附近。
central_claims.what_it_proves: 对于文中自由能、参数与纳米线问题，离散模型能维持具有物理解释且近似恒定的弥散界面宽度。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 这并不说明同一组参数或界面定律可定量预测所有硅形貌、晶向和循环条件。
central_claims.open_question: 针对不同硅相和温度，梯度能系数与双阱参数应如何独立标定？

central_claims.claim: 与开裂相关的表面载荷历程分为两个阶段：早期压缩由 J2 屈服部分释放；随后表层以下继续锂化，使先前形成的富锂外壳像薄膜一样被拉伸，最终承受环向拉应力。
central_claims.evidence_summary: 表面最初受压并发生塑性屈服，随后已锂化外壳约束内部推进界面处的膨胀，使环向应力转为拉伸。
central_claims.what_it_proves: 在轴对称载荷和给定边界条件下，耦合模型能够产生力学上合理的应力符号反转。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 计算没有解析裂纹成核或扩展，也未针对匹配试样定量比较断裂阈值。
central_claims.open_question: 若加入表面缺陷、氧化层和电化学反应动力学，预测的拉伸历程是否会超过实测断裂抗力？

pipeline: 用守恒的归一化锂浓度 ĉ 同时表示锂化程度与晶态/非晶态，并设置富锂极小值为 0.872 的双阱化学自由能。
把总变形分解为化学、塑性和弹性部分；采用随浓度变化的弹性参数计算应力，并用带线性硬化的各向同性 J2 流动演化不可逆变形。
对总自由能求变分得到化学势，以其梯度驱动锂通量，再与质量守恒结合形成应力耦合的 Cahn–Hilliard 方程。
将四阶相场方程拆成两个二阶方程，并在每个隐式时间步用有限元与力学平衡联立求解。
method_understanding.algorithm_pseudocode:
在四分之一纳米线域上初始化 ĉ 与变形。
每个时间步联立求解拆分后的浓度/化学势方程与准静态位移平衡，并更新本构塑性变量。
推进 ĉ 和塑性状态，记录相界面位置、几何形貌及应力。

algorithm_steps.action: 以给定浓度分布和无应力几何初始化四分之一纳米线域。
algorithm_steps.inputs: 半径、初始 ĉ、材料参数与相场参数
algorithm_steps.outputs: 初始浓度、位移和塑性状态

algorithm_steps.action: 施加富锂饱和浓度、化学势零通量、对称约束及外表面无牵引条件。
以弱形式求解化学势、浓度守恒和力学平衡，并更新塑性本构。
algorithm_steps.inputs: 当前浓度、变形和塑性历史
algorithm_steps.outputs: 更新后的 ĉ、化学势、位移与应力

algorithm_steps.action: 采用隐式格式推进时间，并提取界面位置、界面宽度、应力分量和累积塑性应变。
algorithm_steps.outputs: 随时间变化的相、形貌、应力和塑性结果

method_understanding.engineering_derivation_sketch: 从同时惩罚混合浓度与浓度梯度、并包含变形相关弹性能和塑性能的自由能出发。按照论文关于塑性能不依赖归一化浓度的假设，其导数给出 μ_pl=0，因此有效锂化学势由化学/梯度项和弹性项组成。化学势梯度驱动的 Onsager 型通量与质量守恒结合后得到 Cahn–Hilliard 演化；乘法运动学则分别追踪化学膨胀、可恢复弹性和塑性流动。
implementation_details: 数值实现采用 COMSOL、二维三节点三角形单元，每个节点含浓度、化学势和两个位移共四个自由度，时间推进为一阶隐式格式。
利用圆对称性只计算四分之一圆域；参考半径为 70 nm，物理时间步为 2.45 s。

datasets: 论文未发布数据集；验证对象包括理想化 70 nm 硅纳米线计算、原位实验所见的核壳形貌、解析界面宽度估计以及既有非线性扩散模拟。
metrics: 评价量包括相界面位置与尖锐程度、界面宽度、径向/环向/von Mises 应力、应力符号随时间的变化以及累积塑性应变。
main_results: 相场模型维持尖锐核壳界面，再现非线性扩散模型的应力分布趋势，并预测锂化后期的表面环向拉应力。
计算界面宽度随时间保持在解析值附近，而不是像对比扩散模型那样增宽数倍。
ablation_or_comparison_takeaways: 纯弹性与弹塑性曲线的比较表明，屈服显著限制应力幅值并改变其时间历程，因此对大膨胀硅不可忽略塑性。
与非线性扩散模型的剩余差异可能来自塑性定律、网格密度和几何设置，相场应力曲线仍有小幅数值波动。

numeric_results.dataset_or_task: 半径 70 nm 硅纳米线的两相锂化
numeric_results.interpretation: 弥散界面保持预期的纳米级材料长度，而不会随时间持续扩散。
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: 与内部解析估计一致并不能独立标定所有硅电极适用的 κ 或 Δg。

numeric_results.dataset_or_task: 完全锂化硅的本构设置
numeric_results.metric: 由 300% 体积增量换算的终态/初态体积比
numeric_results.interpretation: 有限变形模型在材料点体积达到初始值 4 倍的大膨胀区间内得到检验。
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: 预设膨胀量不能验证本构定律及其路径依赖是否符合某一具体实验。

theory_understanding.problem_formulation: 目标是在约 300% 局部膨胀、塑性流动和应力影响化学势的条件下，模拟富锂非晶壳向贫锂晶态硅纳米线核心推进的尖锐弥散界面。

key_equations.label: 应力耦合 Cahn–Hilliard 演化
key_equations.explanation: 化学项与梯度项产生两相和有限界面，弹性能使 μ 对应力敏感；塑性能虽出现在形式自由能中，但因其浓度导数被假设为零，在本文中不直接驱动输运。

key_equations.label: 弥散界面宽度
key_equations.explanation: 界面宽度由梯度能系数 κ 与双阱势垒 Δg 的竞争决定，提供对比扩散模型所缺少的材料长度尺度。

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: 由总自由能的导数定义化学势。
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: 锂的迁移响应组分梯度、相偏好和机械载荷共同形成的能量代价，而非只响应浓度。

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: 分离化学膨胀、塑性流动与弹性畸变。
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: 这样可描述巨大的不可逆形变，而不迫使弹性应变本身变得不合理。

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: 把尖锐间断转化为能量控制的弥散界面。
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: 梯度惩罚避免数值上无限薄的跳变，双阱则稳定两个体相浓度。

assumptions: 一个标量浓度场同时表示组分与非晶/晶态结构。
化学膨胀各向同性，塑性为体积不变的带线性硬化 J2 流动，扩散时间尺度上始终满足力学平衡。
外表面保持富锂饱和浓度、无牵引且化学势法向通量为零。
key_results: 模型产生持续的核壳两相形貌，向内推进的界面在后期减速。
界面宽度约为 1.12 nm，而对比非线性扩散模型缺少稳定的材料长度尺度。
已锂化外壳约束内部膨胀，使表面环向应力由压缩转为拉伸。
theory_understanding.engineering_proof_sketch: 非凸化学能固定两个优选浓度，梯度项规定过渡代价，二者平衡给出解析界面宽度。富锂物质从外侧生成时，化学膨胀首先造成压缩和塑性流动；界面继续向内推进后，已膨胀外壳限制其下方材料扩张，从而使外壳环向受拉。力学与化学势联立求解，使这一应力历程进入输运驱动力。
limitations: 规则溶液形式仅作为数学双阱，并未被宣称为非晶 LixSi 的微观自由能。
框架包含应力相关输运，但文中未系统研究应力对扩散和反应的迟滞作用。

task_context: 应用对象是晶态硅纳米线首次锂化：富锂非晶 Li3.75Si 壳层跨越约纳米厚界面向近乎未锂化的晶态核心推进。
experimental_setup: 数值算例采用半径 70 nm 的圆形截面，并把浓度界面行为与原位核壳观察比较，把应力场与既有非线性浓度相关扩散模型比较。
富锂组分设为 ĉ=0.872，弹性模量随锂化软化，屈服强度与硬化模量分别取 1.5 GPa 和 1.0 GPa。
constraints: 轴对称、各向同性、表面均匀饱和和无牵引条件排除了晶向、反应界面、接触及缺陷非均匀性。
transfer_limits: 方程可推广至其他发生相变的高容量电极，但若要定量迁移，必须重新标定特定材料的自由能、迁移率、塑性参数和边界条件。
